title: bar: an empty JSON text hides the module instead of printing its JSON (#15346)
body:
Closes #15346.

A custom `"type": "command"` module whose script prints `{"text":"","class":"ok"}` showed that JSON on the bar: `CustomCommandModule.update()` did `outputText = data.text || String(raw || "").trim()`, and an empty string is falsy, so the raw fallback won even though the JSON had parsed.

The choice moves into `shell/plugins/bar/BarModel.js` as `customCommandLabel(raw, data)` — `Bar.qml` already imports that module, so there is no new import — where the existing node harness can reach it. The parsed `text` is the label whenever the JSON has one, empty included; only output with no `text` field, or no JSON at all, shows the raw output. `{"class":"ok"}` and a JSON scalar such as `123` keep behaving as before.

## Testing

`bash test/shell.d/bar-custom-command-output-test.sh` runs eight assertions through `run_node_test`: the empty text, a real text, plain (non-JSON) output, empty output, the three unchanged cases, and that `Bar.qml` calls the shared label so the rule cannot drift back into the QML.

With the old `||` restored the first assertion fails with `expected: ` / `actual:   {"text":"","class":"ok"}`, so it is a guard rather than a restatement of the change.
